subject: Prod Deployment: VPC connectivity clarifications & agreed next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Connors <alex.connors@fintech.example.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-17T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Prod Deployment: VPC connectivity clarifications & agreed next steps

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and the remaining items we need to qualify to get you an accurate Dedicated vs Private VPC proposal (and an on-prem feasibility note):

What we agreed on during call:
- Primary preference: Private VPC (compliance + data residency), with PrivateLink as the preferred connectivity pattern unless there are constraints from your networking/security team.
- Backup option: Reserved Dedicated capacity if Private VPC onboarding timeline is prohibitive.
- Procurement window: you indicated a likely purchase decision in Q2 and asked for network preflight details this week.

Open technical questions / asks (please confirm):
1) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering: Is there a firm constraint preventing AWS PrivateLink? If so, why (cross-account peering policy, transit gateway limits, etc.)?
2) Egress / allowlist: Can you share expected egress IP ranges or confirm if you prefer to allow by PrivateLink service name (no IP allowlist needed)?
3) TLS termination & certs: Will Redwood terminate TLS on our side (we support mutual TLS) or do you require TLS passthrough to an internal proxy?
4) DNS & split-horizon: Do you operate internal DNS for private hostnames? Will CNAMEs be accepted for the PrivateLink endpoint?
5) Network owner contact: please share the networking lead so we can sync on firewall/route details (we need a direct contact for the preflight call).

Attachments: I attached a short one-pager on PrivateLink vs Peering and our preflight checklist (stubs included below).

Next steps (proposed):
- You share network owner and any egress IP ranges OR confirm PrivateLink preference by EOD Thursday.
- We schedule a 30–45m preflight with your network/security and our infra engineer (Grace) next week.
- Upon answers, we will produce a Private VPC statement-of-work and a Dedicated fallback quote.

Thanks — I copied Grace (infra) and Karthik (security) to help on the preflight.

—
Markus Klein
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
attach: privatelink-vs-peering-onepager.pdf (PDF, 230KB)
attach: redwood-network-preflight-checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)
From: Alex Connors <alex.connors@fintech.example.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Ong <sam.ong@fintech.example.com>, procurement@fintech.example.com
Date: 2027-01-18T09:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod Deployment: VPC connectivity clarifications & agreed next steps

Markus — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers from our side and a contact for networking: Sam Ong (cc'd) is our Cloud Networking lead and will own the preflight. He has visibility into our compliance constraints.

Answers / notes:
- PrivateLink preferred: Our security/compliance team prefers PrivateLink because it avoids cross-account route exposure. We do not have a hard block on peering but would need justification (e.g., lower latency or specific traffic patterns).
- Egress allowlist: We don't have static egress IPs published yet from our platform team. If PrivateLink is used we can avoid IP allowlist work. If we must do peering, Sam will surface the egress ranges (may take 2 business days).
- TLS: We prefer Redwood to terminate TLS at the PrivateLink endpoint and mutually authenticate using client certs for the control plane. We will require mTLS for any management API.
- DNS: We run split-horizon internal DNS and can accept PrivateLink DNS entries. We'll need instructions for the CNAME records to map your endpoint into our private zone.

Procurement: procurement@fintech.example.com asked for a ballpark monthly pricing for Dedicated vs Private VPC (estimate acceptable for budgeting). If you can include a simple comparison table, that would help.

Sam — can you take the network/tech preflight? We're aiming for a 30–45m slot next week (Tue/Wed preferred).

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Connors
Head of Product, FinTechCorp
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Connors <alex.connors@fintech.example.com>
Cc: Sam Ong <sam.ong@fintech.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod Deployment: VPC connectivity clarifications & agreed next steps

Alex / Sam — perfect, thanks. Happy to run the preflight focused on PrivateLink first, with peering as a conditional fallback.

Proposed agenda for the preflight (30–45m):
- Introductions & goals (5m)
- High-level architecture we propose (PrivateLink flow, attachment behavior) (10m)
- Network specifics we need from your side: DNS behavior, routing/prefixes, TLS/mTLS handshake and cert provisioning, proxy/NAT behavior (10m)
- Timeline & next steps (5–10m)

Grace will be the primary Redwoods engineer on the call — she can answer routing, TLS, and endpoint configuration. Karthik will own the compliance mapping for mTLS and audit/logging requirements.

Please propose 2 slots that work for your network team next Tue/Wed (Jan 19–20). In parallel we will prepare a 1-page pricing comparison for Dedicated vs Private VPC and a short SOW template so procurement can start internal approvals.

—
Markus
Markus Klein | Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-01-19T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod Deployment: VPC connectivity clarifications & agreed next steps

Hi Sam / Alex — quick note from security/controls perspective so the preflight can be efficient:

Initial preflight data points we'd like to collect (short checklist):
- Preferred connectivity: PrivateLink (confirmed by Alex) — please confirm whether your org requires a break-glass for peering.
- Egress IPs or confirmation that PrivateLink will be used (if peering required, please share CIDR ranges and NAT gateways).
- mTLS: cert rotation cadence, who will act as CA (okta/pki/other), cert distribution method.
- Audit & logs: do you require us to mirror access logs to your SIEM or will you pull from our control plane? (we support both)
- Proxy / TLS passthrough: any existing TLS-terminating proxies (F5/NGINX) in front of the workload that we should be aware of?
- Ports & protocols: we expect 443 for the API; please confirm no additional ports are needed.

If you can reply to the checklist or paste these answers into the HubSpot deal (link below), we can finalize the SOW and network runbook quickly.

HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/8721

Happy to join the preflight — propose Jan 19 10:30am PT or Jan 20 9:00am PT. Sam / Alex, please confirm which slot works and we'll send an invite.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security & Compliance (liaison)
Redwood Inference
